title: Control pocket diary — SOC2 prep fragments
content:
Quick context: personal ramble / working list for control mapping and evidence scouts. Not an official runbook; use as a scratch reference when I triage tickets or prep for audit dry-run.

Top-level goals:
- Get minimal set of artefacts that show recurring evidence for change control, access reviews, and incident logging.
- Identify 3 low-friction gaps we can close before next month to reduce control risk.
- Prepare short answers for SOC2 auditor common asks (retention, privilege escalation, role mapping).

Immediate todo (hands-on):
- Pull last 6 months of deployment events (k8s + infra) for prod clusters: ticket -> trace IDs -> who approved (start with infra repo 1287 PR).
  - Jira: SEC-482 might link to the change window notes, check comments from "ops-oncall".
- Compile access list for "private-deployments" service accounts (who has impersonation): ask SRE to export IAM bindings.
- Find backup runbooks for DB snapshots; are snapshots encrypted with customer KMS keys? if not, escalate.

Draft evidence map (very skeletal):
- Change control: PR + approval + rollout plan + canary metrics snapshot. Source: github PRs, console rollout dashboard screenshot, canary logs (console/observability).
- Access reviews: quarterly email thread + exported access spreadsheet + evidence of remediation (tickets closed).
- Incident management: incident triage notes + postmortem ID + timeline. Need a consistent header format for PMs so auditors can parse.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Hypothesis A: we don’t have a consistent audit trail for config-only changes to model routing policies (console UI edits). If true -> gaps for change-control scope.
- Q: Are personal machines allowed to store ephemeral keys for dedicated accounts? Need policy link. If answer is yes -> must document exceptions and compensating controls.
- Hypothesis B: ephemeral KV caches (redis) are excluded from backup procedures in some private deploys. Check infra inventory.

Notes-to-self for auditor Qs (short answers):
- "How do you ensure only authorized changes reach prod?" -> PR + approval workflow in github; required reviewers for infra; dedicated canary window; rollout policy with auto-fallback. (Need screenshots + snippet of branch protection rules).
- "How do you track privileged access?" -> IAM bindings + monthly review tickets + SSO audit logs retained 90 days (confirm retention window).

Evidence collection checklist (quick):
[ ] GitHub branch protection config (screenshot)
[ ] Canary metrics snapshot (last 2 deploys)
[ ] Access review export (last quarter)
[ ] KMS key rotation log for backups
[ ] Incident PM template example

Quick heuristics when pulling artifacts:
- Prefer dates/timestamps and actor names. If artifact lacks actor, find correlating audit log entry.
- When in doubt, capture a screenshot + filepath + query used (so we can reproduce).
- If evidence is transient (metrics dashboards), export CSV and upload to evidence bucket (secure link).

Potential quick wins (<= 2 days):
- Turn branch protection enforcement on for "infra/prod-config" if not already set. (Ops + Eng infra).
- Add a header to incident PMs that includes "incident id, start ts, detection method, severity" as mandatory fields.
- Create a tiny Confluence template for access review notes so reviewers fill remediation lines.

Weird edge cases to check later:
- Third-party backup providers: do they sign BAA? (Legal check)
- Private deployment air-gapped option: need clarity on evidence collection method when logs are not exported off-site.
- Can we map rollout policies in console to a stable ID auditors can reference? If not, export JSON snapshots.

Slack threads / links to follow up (scratch):
- #trust-ops: thread "kube-deploy-audit" (search Feb 2026)
- #infra: recent convo about "canary windows" (Marta posted a snippet)
- Confluence: CONF-3128 (change control playbook, needs update)

Last-minute checklist before handing to auditor (for me):
- Redact PII from evidence artifacts.
- Ensure evidence files are uploaded to the secure bucket and links are in the Confluence page.
- Draft 3 high-level Q&A lines for legal + GDPR/CCPA overlap.

Notes about tone: keep answers plain, avoid engineering slang in auditor-facing pages. Provide traceable pointers (PR IDs, ticket IDs, timestamps).

Random brainstorm (maybe later):
- Small script to stitch PR -> release -> canary metrics -> revert link. Could automate evidence collection for change-control. Low priority but high ROI for next quarter.

End of pocket diary. Will update after I pull IAM bindings and runbooks (scheduled 2026-02-18).

Fragment history: started as a quick Slack-to-self memo while prepping for dry-run run-through. Kept some choppy lines intentionally to be quick to scan.
